newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma moving inmates out of private Texas jail.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma moving inmates out of private Texas jail.

text.p: Oklahoma prison officials have started transferring inmates out of a privately run Texas jail after uncovering alleged abuse by guards there, a prison spokesman said Tuesday.

The prisoners were being moved out of an east Texas facility operated by Capital Correctional Resources Inc., the same company that runs a Houston-area jail in which one inmate was videotaped being bit by a police dog and another stung with an electric stun gun.

"We had some concerns about the quality of life issue and the use of pepper spray. There seemed to be an inordinate use of pepper spray," Oklahoma Department of Corrections spokesman Jerry Massie said of the decision to move the inmates.

Oklahoma began transferring more than 250 of its inmates back to a state prison in Hinton when beds became available, and plans to repatriate the remaining 210 prisoners by October from a CCRI-run jail in Limestone County, Texas, Massie said.

The state had been paying about $40 a day per inmate to have its prisoners housed in the Texas facility, and Massie said the decision to return the prisoners to Oklahoma was made weeks before the videotape surfaced.
"Our goal is to eventually have all our inmates in Oklahoma. They are Oklahoma inmates, they ought to be in Oklahoma," he said.

More than 400 Missouri prisoners were being transferred out of the CCRI-run Brazoria County Detention Center this week following release of a "training video" showing guards in riot gear abusing inmates during a melee last September.

CCRI, a central Texas company operating the Brazoria jail in Angleton, about 25 miles south of Houston, has three facilities in Texas that house inmates under contracts with Missouri and Oklahoma, prison officials said.
Officials with the Groesbeck, Texas-based CCRI could not be reached for comment.
